verdicts.flaw_description: A named alternative cause reaches all four machines: "The lubricant supply moved from mineral to synthetic grade mid-cycle, and every machine here drew from that supply." A mineral-to-synthetic grease upgrade is itself a well-known driver of longer bearing life, so the 260-410 extra hours cannot be attributed to the redesigned bearing.

The measured population is narrower than the claim: "Rates cover the patients whose whole stay ran under the protocol, and a quarter of each ward's patients had spells outside the protocol." A quarter of each ward is excluded from the counts, so the 6-11 percent falls describe a selected fully-covered subgroup, not the ward infection rate the claim is about.

A confound reaches every cohort: "The free trial ran eighteen days, up from ten in the earlier period, and every cohort here signed up on that trial." Week-two (day-14) retention is measured inside the new 18-day trial but after the old 10-day trial expired, so the 3-6 point lift is explained by the trial extension rather than the onboarding email.

The figures cover a narrower population than the claim: "Figures cover the orders rung up at the new prices, and about a fifth of each line's orders were rung up at the old prices." One order in five is excluded from the measurement, so the 4-7 percent lift is for a selected subset of orders, not revenue per order for the line after the pricing change.

Two of the four cases have outcome dates before the start date: cohort one "started 4 April; by 29 March resting heart rate ran 5 bpm below" and cohort three "started 5 October; by 30 September ... ran 6 bpm below." Those drops were recorded before the app was enrolled, so they cannot be effects of it.
